target: Scheduled-passenger DD/FD certificate revenue passenger miles, in millions, with the preserved four-market WAC crosswalk. Served traffic is an endogenous demand proxy, not unconstrained demand or consolidated UAL traffic.
state_model: Log RPM = carrier-market offset + shared within-market calendar-month effect + local-level state + Gaussian measurement error. Twelve local levels follow a random walk; process innovations correlate across the three carriers in the same market. Initial covariance is identity. Missing/unreleased observations receive no update.
estimation: At each month-end issue date, require every initial 2013-19 observation to be released. A complete market target requires both selected DD and FD scope releases, including scopes with no contributing segments; use the latest of contributor and both scope publication dates. Expand the fit with observations available by that cutoff only. Ridge estimates offsets/market seasonality; conditional innovation likelihood selects process and measurement variances on the declared finite grids, separately for each pooling candidate. No global continuous-MLE claim.
baseline_rule: Persistence uses the most recent released observation in the target calendar month. Fixed mean uses only the initial sample. AR uses log lag 1, log lag 12, carrier-market offsets and market calendar-month effects; it recursively bridges the release gap without target observations.
selection_metric: Lowest equal-weight mean MASE across 48 carrier/market/horizon cells on identical eligible forecasts. Scaling is each series' initial-sample mean absolute lag-12 RPM difference. Deterministic ties use declared pooling order. No locked target access.
uncertainty: Native Gaussian/lognormal predictive intervals conditional on fixed fitted parameters are uncalibrated. No pathwise parameter uncertainty, causal elasticity, pricing response, joint coverage or extreme-shock guarantee. Native interval coverage/width/CRPS are descriptive and conditional; compare sources separately from sampling/model uncertainty.
vintage: Current-download rolling releases with filename publication proxies. Reviewed histories/targets use present-day hindsight quality knowledge. No independently captured historical bytes/timestamps or point-in-time performance claim.
scope: Same-table certificate scheduled-passenger DD/FD traffic. Foreign-to-foreign coverage, consolidated marketed regional flying, fare/yield matching, unconstrained demand and simulator integration remain unresolved. No SEC/Form 41 revenue denominator or synthetic fare target.
history_rule: For every rolling issue, select its exact origin observation versions, never filter a final panel. Annual comparison reconstructs the original annual-only final panel by its declared availability gates and remains separately labeled. Native and reviewed forecasts retain separate fits. Reuse identical native rolling predictions when only evaluation targets change.
initial_rule: Freeze seasonal means and MASE scales from the first rolling origin with the complete 12-series by 84-month 2013-19 grid released. Use exactly this initial anchor across all histories/cases; later revisions cannot alter this fixed baseline.
evaluation_rule: Every case retains identical requested issue/carrier/market/horizon/target keys and targets. Primary scorecards use identical global supported keys across all six models/four cases. Report failures separately and require all 48 comparison cells represented; no locked 2024+ access.
research_gate: Corrected certificate traffic is not unconstrained demand, pricing, calibration, a deployed policy or investment validation. Residual FF/regional/issuer boundaries remain open.
failure_protocol: Keep all requested forecasts with exact model support/failure statuses. Preserve the existing AR absolute-log bound of 40 and all model grids/ridges. Primary point comparisons use the intersection of finite, supported forecast keys across every candidate/baseline and every source case; report requested/supported/excluded counts and horizon/regime failures. Do not clip or impute failed forecasts, hide them, or claim the common subset establishes whole-domain robustness.
